jonny-desktop.task: meristem loot drops: wire items.drop_tables so killing an enemy rolls its table and spawns the item, closing the fight-loot-equip loop
jonny-desktop.note: DONE + PUSHED, awaiting merge. PR #14 (branch feat/loot-drops, commit 35f3bb8), CI green ubuntu + windows py3.12. PR #13 merged as e1ca2de first, so not stacked. CLOSES THE FIGHT-LOOT-EQUIP LOOP. items.drop_tables had been authorable since the items schema was written and compiled to nothing, so gear could only be found by hand-placing it in a level. Now the table is baked into the Game autoload as enemy_id -> {drops, nothing}; an enemy's death rolls it and spawns the winning item where it fell. Two required details, not stylistic: the pickup is parented to get_tree().current_scene rather than to the enemy (queue_free would take the loot with it), and the roll happens BEFORE queue_free (a freed node has no position to drop at). All three AI templates now bake ENEMY_ID and call drop_loot; there is a test asserting all three do, because that death block is duplicated per template and is exactly what gets updated in one and forgotten in the others. New optional nothing_weight on a drop table - without it EVERY kill drops something. It sits in the SAME weighted pool as the drops rather than being a separate pre-roll, so one set of numbers describes the whole distribution and an author reads the odds straight off the table. Loot-only items now get a pickup scene: drop_loot loads pickup_<id>.tscn by name at runtime and only PLACED items used to get one, so an item no level places would have silently spawned nothing; a droppable item with no sprite is refused at compile time so that failure is a build error rather than an unnoticed nothing on some later kill. VERIFIED with a new loot_drop assertion that kills through take_damage (not by calling drop_loot directly, so the death path itself is proven): the slime drops a sword at exactly (48,48) in Godot 4.6. It only derives for a table with ONE guaranteed drop, because a weighted roll is not deterministic and an assertion that passes most of the time is worse than none. Suite 204 passed with MERISTEM_GODOT set (six assertions green), 198 without as CI runs - verified in a fresh shell, since the env var persists within a single PowerShell call. Decision recorded as dec-018-57b3. STILL NOT WIRED: narrative, economy, items.rarity_tiers (so rarity has no effect on drop odds despite looking like it should). No inventory or unequip - a second weapon silently replaces the first. Only atk/def bonuses are consumed, so an item granting hp or spd validates and does nothing. Dropped items land exactly where the enemy died, which can be inside a wall or on water since there is no placement validity check. Also outstanding: turn_based_combat emits nothing, no attack animation in the humanoid archetype, and CI does not set MERISTEM_GODOT so it validates generated code by string and structure but never by behaviour. RECOMMENDED NEXT: merge PR #14, then consider wiring MERISTEM_GODOT into CI (Godot has a headless Linux binary) so the six engine assertions guard every push rather than only local runs - that is the highest-leverage remaining item, since three real bugs this session were invisible to string checks.
